ΔG = ΔH − TΔS
Feasible reaction = ΔG is negative or zero
Smaller, more highly charged ions = More exothermic lattice energy

games.title: Electrochemistry — find the pair
games.source:
Standard hydrogen electrode = Reference electrode with E° = 0.00 V
Salt bridge = Completes the circuit and allows ion movement
More positive E° = Stronger oxidising agent
More negative E° = Stronger reducing agent
E°cell = E°(reduction) − E°(oxidation)
Faraday constant = 96 500 C mol⁻¹
Charge passed in electrolysis = Current × time (Q = It)
Nernst equation = Shows how E changes with concentration
Fuel cell = Converts chemical energy of a fuel directly into electricity
Standard conditions = 298 K, 1 mol dm⁻³, 101 kPa

games.title: Acid–base equilibria and solubility — find the pair
games.source:
Ka = Acid dissociation constant
pKa = −log Ka
pH = −log[H⁺]
Kw = 1.00 × 10⁻¹⁴ mol² dm⁻⁶ at 298 K
Buffer = Resists changes in pH on adding small amounts of acid or base
Acidic buffer = Weak acid and its conjugate base
Ksp = Solubility product of a sparingly soluble salt
Common ion effect = Reduces solubility of a salt
Equivalence point = Moles of acid and base exactly react
Half-equivalence point = pH equals pKa

games.title: Reaction kinetics — find the pair
games.source:
Rate constant = k in the rate equation
Order of reaction = Power of a concentration term in the rate equation
Zero order = Rate does not depend on concentration
First order = Constant half-life
Second order = Rate quadruples when concentration doubles
Rate-determining step = Slowest step in the mechanism
Homogeneous catalyst = Same phase as reactants
Heterogeneous catalyst = Different phase from reactants
Arrhenius equation = Relates k to temperature and Ea
Half-life = Time for concentration to halve

games.title: Transition elements — crossword
games.source:
LIGAND = Species that donates a lone pair to a metal ion
BIDENTATE = Ligand forming two dative bonds, like ethanedioate
CHELATE = Complex with a ring formed by a multidentate ligand
OCTAHEDRAL = Shape of a complex with six ligands
COMPLEMENTARY = Colour seen is the one opposite the colour absorbed
CISPLATIN = Square planar anticancer complex of platinum
HAEM = Iron-containing group in haemoglobin
VANADIUM = Element whose oxide catalyses the Contact process

games.title: A Level organic chemistry — find the pair
games.source:
Benzene = Delocalised π electrons in a ring
Nitration of benzene = Conc. HNO3 and conc. H2SO4 at 55 °C
Friedel–Crafts alkylation = Halogenoalkane with AlCl3 catalyst
Phenol = Reacts with bromine water without a catalyst
Phenylamine = Made by reducing nitrobenzene with Sn and conc. HCl
Diazonium salt = Made with NaNO2 and HCl below 10 °C
Azo dye = Formed by coupling a diazonium ion with phenol
Acyl chloride = Reacts vigorously with water to give HCl fumes
Amide = Formed from an acyl chloride and ammonia
Condensation polymer = Polyester or polyamide

games.title: Analytical techniques — find the pair
games.source:
Mass spectrometry = Gives the molecular ion peak and Mr
M+1 peak = Used to find the number of carbon atoms
M+2 peak = Shows the presence of Cl or Br
Infrared spectroscopy = Identifies functional groups by bond vibrations
Broad peak 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ = O–H in a carboxylic acid
Peak near 1700 cm⁻¹ = C=O bond
Carbon-13 NMR = Number of carbon environments
Proton NMR splitting = n+1 rule
TMS = Reference standard at δ = 0 ppm
D2O = Removes O–H and N–H peaks in proton NMR

games.title: A Level key words — quiz
games.source:
What is a "ligand"?
*A molecule or ion that donates a lone pair to a central metal ion
A metal ion with variable oxidation states
A catalyst for transition metals
A type of isomer

What is meant by "order of reaction" with respect to a reactant?
*The power to which its concentration is raised in the rate equation
The number of molecules in the equation
The slowest step of a mechanism
The number of products formed

What is a "buffer solution"?
*A solution that resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or alkali are added
A solution with pH 7
A strong acid mixed with a strong base
A solution that changes colour at the end point

What is "entropy"?
*A measure of the dispersal of energy and disorder in a system
The heat content of a system
The energy needed to start a reaction
The free energy of a reaction

What is a "chiral centre"?
*A carbon atom attached to four different groups
A carbon with a double bond
A carbon in a benzene ring
A carbon attached to two identical groups

What is "standard electrode potential"?
*The EMF of a half-cell relative to the standard hydrogen electrode under standard conditions
The voltage of any battery
The charge on one mole of electrons
The rate of electrolysis

What is a "transition element"?
*A d-block element that forms one or more stable ions with an incomplete d subshell
Any metal in the d-block
An element in Group 2
An element with a full d subshell

What is "lattice energy"?
*The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic compound forms from its gaseous ions
The energy to melt one mole of ionic compound
The energy to dissolve one mole of a salt
The energy released when atoms form molecules

games.title: Polymers and organic synthesis — find the pair
games.source:
Addition polymer = Formed from alkene monomers with no other product
Polyester = Formed from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid
Polyamide = Formed from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
Nylon-6,6 = Polyamide from hexanedioic acid and hexane-1,6-diamine
Kevlar = Aromatic polyamide with strong hydrogen bonding
Protein = Natural polyamide of amino acids
Biodegradable polymer = Can be broken down by microorganisms
Poly(ethene) = Non-biodegradable addition polymer
Retrosynthesis = Working backwards from the target molecule
Nitrile = Increases the carbon chain length by one

games.title: Transition elements and redox titrations — find the pair
games.source:
MnO4⁻ titration = Self-indicating: purple to colourless at the end point
MnO4⁻ to Mn²⁺ = Gains 5 electrons
Cr2O7²⁻ to Cr³⁺ = Gains 6 electrons
Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ = Loses 1 electron
Iodine–thiosulfate titration = Starch indicator added near the end point
Mole ratio S2O3²⁻ : I2 = 2 : 1
Mole ratio MnO4⁻ : Fe²⁺ = 1 : 5
Variable oxidation states = Similar energies of 3d and 4s electrons
Heterogeneous catalysis = Iron in the Haber process
Coloured ions = Partially filled d orbitals split by ligands

games.title: Electrochemistry and equilibria — practice — crossword
games.source:
ELECTRODE = Conductor where oxidation or reduction occurs
ANODE = Electrode where oxidation takes place
CATHODE = Electrode where reduction takes place
FARADAY = Constant equal to about 96 500 coulombs per mole
PLATINUM = Inert metal used in the hydrogen half-cell
VOLTMETER = Instrument with high resistance to measure cell EMF
SOLUBILITY = Maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a solvent
EQUILIBRIUM = State where forward and reverse rates are equal

games.title: Planning an investigation — find the pair
games.source:
Independent variable = The variable you deliberately change
Dependent variable = The variable you measure
Control variables = Variables kept constant
Hypothesis = Prediction that can be tested
Fume cupboard = Used for toxic or volatile substances
Goggles = Protect eyes from corrosive chemicals
Range of values = At least five different values of the independent variable
Repeat readings = Allow a mean to be calculated
Gas syringe = Measures gas volume to ±0.5 cm³
Data-logger = Records measurements automatically over time

games.title: Data analysis and uncertainty — find the pair
games.source:
Line of best fit = Straight line or smooth curve through the data
Gradient = Change in y ÷ change in x
Intercept = Value where the line crosses an axis
Worst acceptable line = Used to find the uncertainty in the gradient
Anomalous point = Ignored when drawing the line of best fit
Error bar = Shows the uncertainty of a plotted point
Proportional = Straight line through the origin
Inversely proportional = y increases as x decreases, y × x constant
Log graph = Used to find the order of a reaction
Correlation = Trend between two variables

games.title: Experimental design terms — quiz
games.source:
Which describes a "control variable"?
*A variable kept constant so it does not affect the results
The variable that is measured
The variable that is changed deliberately
A variable that has no effect on anything

Why should a thermostatically controlled water bath be used in a rate experiment?
*To keep the temperature constant
To increase the reaction rate
To measure the volume of gas
To dissolve the reactants

What is the purpose of a "blank" in colorimetry?
*To set zero absorbance using the solvent alone
To increase absorbance
To calibrate the burette
To act as an indicator

Which improvement reduces percentage error in measuring a mass of 0.20 g?
*Use a larger mass
Use a less precise balance
Repeat with the same small mass only
Weigh it in an open beaker in a draught

Why is a lid placed on a polystyrene cup in a calorimetry experiment?
*To reduce heat loss to the surroundings
To keep the solution sterile
To stop the thermometer moving
To increase the temperature change

Which method gives the most accurate volume of 25.0 cm³ of solution?
*Volumetric pipette
Measuring cylinder
Beaker
Conical flask

What is meant by a "fair test"?
*Only the independent variable is changed; others are controlled
All variables are changed together
The experiment is repeated once
The results support the hypothesis

Which is the best way to make the end point of a titration clearer?
*Place the flask on a white tile
Add more indicator after the end point
Use a coloured background
Swirl less often

games.title: Graphs and gradients — find the pair
games.source:
Rate from a curve = Gradient of a tangent
Concentration–time straight line = Zero order reaction
Rate–concentration straight line through origin = First order reaction
Rate–concentration curve upwards = Second order reaction
ln k against 1/T = Gradient equals −Ea/R
Cooling curve plateau = Change of state
Plot axes = Use more than half the grid
Label axes = Quantity / unit
Plotting points = Use small crosses accurately to half a square
Units of gradient = Units of y divided by units of x

games.title: Evaluating experiments — find the pair
games.source:
Heat loss = Main error in simple calorimetry
Gas escaping before the bung is replaced = Low volume of gas recorded
Using a gas syringe instead of collecting over water = Avoids gas dissolving
Repeating the experiment = Increases reliability
Using a more precise balance = Reduces percentage uncertainty
Using a burette instead of a measuring cylinder = More precise volumes
Reaction too fast to time = Dilute the reactants or lower the temperature
Subjective end point = Use a colorimeter or pH probe
Impure reactant = Gives a lower percentage yield
Incomplete reaction = Heat for longer or use excess reagent

games.title: Choosing apparatus — quiz
games.source:
Which apparatus measures 23.45 cm³ of a solution most precisely?
*Burette
Measuring cylinder
Beaker
Conical flask

Which apparatus should be used to make 250.0 cm³ of a standard solution?
*Volumetric flask
Beaker
Measuring cylinder
Conical flask

Which piece of apparatus is used to follow a reaction by mass loss?
*Top-pan balance
Gas syringe
Burette
Thermometer

Which apparatus measures absorbance of a coloured solution?
*Colorimeter
pH meter
Gas syringe
Burette

Which apparatus is best to heat a solid strongly to constant mass?
*Crucible with lid on a pipe-clay triangle
Beaker on a tripod
Test tube in a water bath
Conical flask with a bung

Which apparatus allows heating under reflux?
*Round-bottomed flask with a vertical condenser
Beaker with a watch glass
Evaporating basin
Open boiling tube

Which apparatus is used to separate two immiscible liquids?
*Separating funnel
Büchner funnel
Burette
Volumetric pipette

Which is used to filter crystals under reduced pressure?
*Büchner funnel and flask
Separating funnel
Evaporating basin
Condenser
